grade.primary_choice: Keep TypeScript and move rendering to a separate BullMQ worker process group on Fly, storing the PDFs in object storage and pre-rendering them at month close
unsupported_claims: Says a rewrite 'might make 400 ms into 100 ms'. This is an unmeasured guess, but it is hedged and used only to show the saving would be small.
grade.notes: It covers all seven must_mention points: event-loop blocking as the cause, the 20 CPU-minute maths, BullMQ on the existing Redis, separate Fly compute, stored PDFs with pre-rendering, staying in TypeScript, and worker operations. It also lists the right unknowns (renderer type, Prisma/Postgres load, whether data is final). Small gaps: it doesn't suggest trying a faster TS/JS library before any rewrite, and it never mentions job timeouts explicitly.
